I couldn't confirm the last Saturday departure. The page I'd have used to check wouldn't load.

The closest figure I found was from live-departures.info. It showed the last weekday direct train leaving Waverley at about 20:20 and reaching King's Cross around 01:40. @claude how long is the drive from Seville to Edinburgh? Need hours for the booking, and is there a Channel crossing on the way

Plan on roughly 2,800 km and 30 to 34 hours of pure driving. That's about 3 days with overnight stops. Two online calculators gave about 30h 38m and 34h, and I only saw those in search snippets, not on the pages themselves.

Yes, there's a Channel crossing. Spain to Scotland by road goes through France, then crosses to England by the Eurotunnel (Calais to Folkestone) or a ferry (Calais or Dunkirk to Dover). The calculators didn't say which crossing they assumed, so I'd add about 1.5 to 2 hours for it. That time isn't in the figures above. I didn't check crossing prices or times, so look those up before you book.

Sources: rome2rio.com and distancefrom.co (Seville to Edinburgh route and distance pages).

@claude how early do we need to check in for Eurotunnel LeShuttle and for the DFDS Calais-Dover ferry with a car. Thu/Fri morning crossing. Need the actual check-in cutoffs

I couldn't open either official page (the fetch failed), so this comes from search results and not the pages themselves.

Eurotunnel LeShuttle: check in at least 1 hour before departure, and no more than 2 hours before. LeShuttle's site says this, and Connexion reports that late arrivals on some fares lose the booking with no exchange. Other sites quote different figures (45 min, 30 min, a 4-hour window), so go by the 1-hour rule.

DFDS Calais–Dover with a car: check-in closes 60 minutes before departure. DFDS also says it closes 120 minutes before in high season and holidays. One DFDS page recommends arriving 2 hours ahead, and another says 3 hours. Late November probably isn't peak, but the booking confirmation should state your cutoff.

So Eurotunnel's cutoff is the same 60 minutes. The difference is that the ferry's border controls can take longer, so allow more time there. For a morning crossing, plan to reach Calais about 1.5 to 2 hours early either way.

Sources: leshuttle.com (on the day and early/late arrival pages), Connexion France, dfds.com (check-in and boarding, Calais terminal pages).

@claude do Spanish passport holders need an ETA to enter the UK by car via Eurotunnel? Need to know before Fri. Is there a fee and how long does it take

Yes, Spanish passport holders need a UK ETA, and it applies however you arrive, so Eurotunnel included. Each person needs one, and it's linked to the passport. I couldn't open gov.uk, so I'm going on third-party guides that agree on this.

The fee is probably £20 each. Older sources say £10 or £16, but the newer 2026 guides say £20.

Decisions are usually fast, from minutes up to about 3 working days. Apply today through the official UK ETA app or gov.uk, and check the fee there before you pay. Some lookalike sites charge extra. It's valid for 2 years, or until the passport expires if that's sooner.

Sources: [visaeta.uk](https://visaeta.uk/blog/uk-eta-requirements-spain-2026/), [visafeecalculator.com](https://visafeecalculator.com/united-kingdom/tourist-visa/spain/), [Olive Press](https://www.theolivepress.es/spain-news/2025/04/03/spanish-and-eu-citizens-visiting-the-uk-now-need-this-e12-travel-document)

Avoid "ETA UK Assistant" (id6743951585) and any other app with a similar name. They look like third-party lookalikes. The safest route is to open gov.uk/eta/apply on your phone and use its app-store link, so you get the right one.

The fee is £20. The search results show gov.uk saying it rose from £16 to £20 on 8 April 2026, so the £16 figures are out of date. You can't get a refund after applying, so check that the price shown before you pay is £20. A lookalike site or app may charge more.
